recommendation: Minimum-touch / AI-native operating model (routine work runs without human touch; humans handle exceptions and legally reserved decisions)
decision_posture: Experimental for the operating model inside a bounded cohort; Guardrail for every control it touches
owner: Product owner (claim); CFO (cost case); sponsor compliance officer (control floors)
executive_understanding: Minimum-touch is a coherent design direction whose cost case rests entirely on assumed exception share (e) and minutes per exception (m); no operating measurement exists, and the documented AI-native cost advantage disappears inside the documented parameter ranges.
clarity_snapshot: The load-bearing quantity is e*m, not the number of routine touches. Under base labour the AI-native per-account advantage over the Fidelity-derived frontier is lost at e*m of about 41; under pessimistic labour at about 24 [S economic-model]. The expected case is e*m = 3.6 (8% x 45 min) [A].
current_understanding: Known: the per-account exception cost formula is linear in A, g, e, m and inverse in H [S]. Known: expected/low/high exception cost per account is $50/$9/$546 at 100k accounts [S, assumption-driven]. Known: invariant-bearing steps must stay synchronous and deterministic, AI observations are never authoritative (ADR-EVA-001). Not known: any measured e, m, rework or displaced-work value for this platform.

backlog age of consequential queues
after-hours incident response time
monitoring_plan.threshold: any day in the roster with an SoD role uncovered two-deep; any SoD waiver
monitoring_plan.trigger_claim: roster coverage gaps predict control failure better than headcount
monitoring_plan.response: add cover (fractional/outsourced with sponsor delegation) or hold the affected command class
monitoring_plan.trigger_reassessment: if gaps occur without incidents for a year, check whether the role pairing is actually required

reassessment_plan: Derive the floor from a roster model (UNB-SMP-CLR-001, proposed here) before stating any target
Reconsider if R1 uses the manual reconciliation fallback
Reconsider if any regulator or auditor expectation of staffing is identified
learning_priorities: Build a day-by-day roster for Dec 24-Jan 2 with SoD pairs and independence
Distinguish operational floor (sponsor) from engineering/agent-owner floor (platform) per review-arch-econ A2
recommended_next_posture: Do not adopt a below-floor staffing target. Replace "the floor" with a roster-derived minimum by role and day, then test automation against it.
current_best_understanding: There is no validated staffing floor to go below. The defensible lower bound is set by two-deep coverage of the payment and sanctions chain on the worst calendar days, which the operations review puts at roughly ten people, and which automation reduces only if it also reduces the number of distinct independent roles.
independence_note: Same-model analysis; not independent validation (Clarity research README:19-21; EDF claim policy Independence).
